answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public smart contract before it can earn fees or vote; reports of duplicate control are checked against signed messages and on-chain links, and a successful challenge slashes the bond and distributes part to the challenger. Creating many identities therefore multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying one operator’s real influence. A nadir in reputation can block access to a bridge or lagoon market, but the core deterrent is that every fake identity needs separately exposed collateral.
